title: On quantum channels: extreme points, topology, and categorical properties
authors: J. M. S. T. da Silva
abstract: In this thesis, quantum channels are studied from the point of view of Mathematics. We studied the CPTP (completely positive trace preserving) and UCPTP channels, the latter being the unital channels. In both cases, the sets are compact convex, so they are the closure of their extreme points. We constructed extreme CPTP maps for every possible rank. We also constructed extreme UCPTP maps with rank 2 for each possible dimension. For ranks of at least 3, we constructed extreme UCPTP maps for many dimensions and ranks. We also proved that the tensor product of extreme CPTP maps is an extreme CPTP map. For UCPTP maps, we proved that the same is not always true, with many counterexamples. It is known that the category of CPTP maps is semicartesian. We add to this a classification of binary products. We proved that products only exist in trivial cases. For binary coproducts, we obtained the dimensions they should have, if they exist. In both cases, topological techniques were used. For this reason, we also investigated the topology of the closure of the set of extreme points of the CPTP maps. Topological invariants can be computed from decompositions of a space such as CW structures. These are a type of decomposition in which the space is expressed as a gluing of balls. In the search for a CW structure for the closure of the set of extreme CPTP maps, we obtained a partial decomposition that resembles a CW structure of the complex projective space.
summary: This thesis provides a deep mathematical study of quantum channels (CPTP maps), treating them as objects within abstract mathematical structures. It characterizes the extreme points of these sets and explores their topological and categorical relationships. The work is fundamental for understanding the mathematical limits and structure of quantum operations.
main_problem: The paper mathematically analyzes quantum channels (CPTP maps), focusing on characterizing their extreme points, topological structure, and categorical properties.
main_result: It establishes that the sets of CPTP and UCPTP maps are compact convex sets, constructing extreme maps for various ranks and proving specific properties regarding the tensor product and existence of products/coproducts.
method: The work employs advanced mathematical tools, including topological techniques (CW structures), category theory (monoidal categories), and functional analysis applied to quantum operations.
model_or_system: The model is the quantum channel, mathematically represented by Completely Positive Trace-Preserving (CPTP) maps acting on density matrices in finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces.
key_observables: The primary observables are the quantum channels themselves, characterized by their extreme points, Choi-rank, and structural properties.
important_parameters: The dimensionality of the Hilbert space ($d$) and the rank of the maps are key parameters explored in the construction of extreme examples.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the mathematical framework of Hilbert spaces and the assumption that the sets of quantum channels form compact convex sets.
figures_summary: The notes indicate the presentation of extensive tables detailing parameters for numerous concrete examples of extreme UCPTP maps derived from various mathematical constructions.
paper_structure: The paper systematically reviews CPTP/UCPTP maps, details the structure of the category of CPTP maps, presents constructions and properties of extreme CPTP maps, and concludes with topological investigations into the closure of the extreme point set.
why_interesting: This is highly relevant as it provides the rigorous mathematical backbone for understanding noise and dissipation in open quantum systems, which is central to quantum information theory and quantum optics.
